concepts.title: Boston’s Molasses Flood: The Warning Signs Were Visible
concepts.description:
In January 1919, a huge molasses tank in Boston’s North End leaked before it burst. The flood killed 21 people and injured 150. This short documentary follows the warning signs neighbors could see, the disaster that followed, and the court investigation that found the tank structurally weak and held its owners responsible.

The rupture happened in a moment. Establishing responsibility took six years.

concepts.title: The 1919 Molasses Flood That Swept Through Boston
concepts.description:
On January 15, 1919, a giant molasses tank burst in Boston’s North End. A fast, heavy flood swept through the neighborhood, killing 21 people and injuring 150. This film recounts the disaster and the long investigation that followed, including the finding that the tank was structurally weak and its owners were responsible.

concepts.title: Why Boston’s Molasses Tank Burst—and Who Was Held Responsible
concepts.description:
After Boston’s 1919 molasses flood, the company suggested a possible bomb. A court-appointed auditor instead found the tank structurally weak and held its owners responsible. This documentary traces the visible leaks, the catastrophic flood that killed 21 and injured 150, and the six-year path to that finding—without claiming that every detail of the rupture mechanism is settled.

#BostonHistory #MolassesFlood #EngineeringHistory

Avoid fake readable fine print. Include the exact large headline WHO WAS TO BLAME? in broad rounded, slightly irregular, dimensional paper letters with soft shadows, legible at 320x180. Paper diorama with tactile fibers, layered cut edges, thickness, contact shadows and focused light. The composition must read as an investigation into a tank found structurally weak, not a claim that a bomb caused the failure or that the exact initiating mechanism is known. brief.visual_intent: Frame the aftermath as an accountability question. It differs from A's warning-focused leak and B's immediate disaster spectacle.

comparison.A: What was the warning? Visible pre-failure leak; strongest match to the script's opening and its warning/responsibility angle.
comparison.B: What did the flood do? The force and scale of the event itself.
comparison.C: Who was responsible? The post-disaster finding and accountability question.
comparison.selection_rationale: Choose A as the primary title/thumbnail pair because the script opens on visible leakage and closes on the distinction between immediate failure and six years to establish responsibility. It presents the film's distinctive angle without claiming certainty about the precise rupture mechanism or using disaster imagery as spectacle.
